proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a pointwise mixed-rate selector audit for two fixed grids and a matching finite-sample honest-interval rate on a specified public class. A row-zero drift error and four other panel findings were repaired; the final D0 mathematical recheck passed with no open core statements. D0.5 still judged the contribution subfield rather than field, so formalization was not started; a field-level successor would need a materially broader theorem or a new anchor.
tldr: The anchor paper's treated fixed-quantile hypotheses admit the shifted-uniform witness with \(\gamma_1=3/2\), marginal treated density one at the median, a uniform endpoint conditional limit, and the required uniform local-mass bound. On that source-domain witness, the published full-range grid and shared quadratic correction mix Gaussian and Poisson rows; the fixed \(B=1000\) half-sample dispersion selector chooses \(k=2\) for \(L=8\) and \(k=8\) for \(L=100\), while positive clipping drift dominates its selected dispersion. Coverage tends to zero for this note's fixed-multiple dispersion-centered interval, and this point-witness counterexample transfers to every larger class containing the witness. Separately, a positive-score interval has finite-sample \(90\%\) coverage and maximal expected length \(O(n^{-3/7})\) on the public class defined by bounded outcomes, an interior median, a local density lower margin, and endpoint Lipschitz regularity. A matching two-point lower pair also satisfies the anchor treated fixed-quantile conditions, so the \(n^{-3/7}\) rate is minimax optimal both on the public class and on the source-relevant intersection.
